En una entrevista concedida el miércoles a la agencia de noticias Associated Press (AP), el comisionado general de la Agencia de Naciones Unidas para los Refugiados Palestinos (UNRWA), Philippe Lazzarini, dijo que no existe “absolutamente ningún lugar seguro” en la asediada Franja de Gaza para los civiles, ni siquiera en los refugios de la ONU, así como las llamadas “zonas seguras” designadas por el propio Israel.

Al desarrollar su postura, el funcionario indicó que, desde el estallido de la guerra en Gaza, más de 80 instalaciones de la ONU en la Franja de Gaza que albergan a civiles han sido atacadas “directa o indirectamente”.

De acuerdo con el jefe de la UNRWA, más de 220 palestinos murieron en tales agresiones y 130 de los empleados de la ONU también perdieron la vida en estos bombardeos.

“Creo que el flagrante desprecio de las instalaciones de la ONU (…) requerirá una investigación independiente en el futuro”, subrayó Lazzarini, al respecto.

De igual modo, declaró que los refugios gestionados por la ONU, que actualmente albergan a más de un millón de personas desplazadas, se encuentran en “condiciones sanitarias totalmente superpobladas y atroces”.

Esto mientras, la Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (UNOCHA), ha declarado este jueves que más del 80 % de la población de Gaza, de 2,3 millones de habitantes, ha sido desplazada internamente, y la mayoría ha viajado al sur de la franja después de que se le ordenara evacuar el norte.


Israel inició su campaña de agresiones a Gaza, el pasado 7 de octubre, tras ser sorprendido por la operación palestina Tormenta Al-Agsa. Desde entonces, al menos 16 248 palestinos han sido asesinados, la mayoría de ellos mujeres y niños, mientras que más de 43 616 han resultado heridos.

압도적인 피지컬을 통해 점유율을 가져가 측면으로 양질의 패스를 뿌린다는 전술이었다.

그야말로 아수라장.

그와 중에 무너진 수비라인 틈으로 쇄도하는 폴란드의 한 선수가 있었다.

야로스와프 카친스키(Jarosław Kaczy?ski).

왜, 사람들이 우스갯소리로 하는 말이 있었다.

는 개뿔.

과연 이게 성인팀에서도 먹힐지는 모르겠지만 아무렴 지금 당장은 좋았다.

Идею универсальной электронной книги, её концепцию в полной мере изложил в середине 40-х годов «отец гипертекста» Веннивер Буш. Идея электронных книг обоснована: не нужно будет носить с собой «увесистые» книги, и места на полках они не занимают. 
Совсем недавно, в начальный период широкого распространения интегральных схем, было предпринято несколько попыток выпустить электронные книги. Но вглядываться в тусклый маленький экран размером с почтовую марку не доставляло удовольствия. Электронная книга не могла похвалиться достижениями: качество текста на экране не сравнимо с качеством печати на бумаге. И еще неудобство, может быть, самое важное для пользователя: до недавнего времени массового Интернета не существовало. 
В 1999 году было объявлено о скорой готовности электронных книг, которые выгодно отличались от конкурирующих изделий качеством изображения и длительностью непрерывного питания от аккумуляторов. Теперь ясно, что у проблемы электронных книг несколько граней. Во-первых, сложность производства терминалов (устройств для хранения и вывода текстов на экран) с необходимыми потребительскими качествами. Во-вторых, аспект защиты интеллектуальной собственности (авторского права) в Интернете. Наконец, неосязаемые эстетические свойства, обретённые бумажными книгами на протяжении столетий развития полиграфии, чего нет у электронных книг.
Книги из бумаги с твёрдыми переплётами представляют собой образцы высочайшего мастерства, отточенного на протяжении многих столетий. Того самого мастерства, которое может претендовать на вечность.

Для того, чтобы стать нашими повседневными спутниками, электронным книгам придётся овладеть всеми тайнами своих бумажных предшественников. Pop was originally launched on 29 May 2003 by Chart Show Channels (CSC) Media Group as Toons&Tunes. Toons&Tunes was then later rebranded as its current name, Pop (formerly stylized as pop and POP!) in the following month.

In the channel's early years, links were presented by Rorry, a lime green dragon with a Scottish accent, who was animated live. He was accompanied by Purrdy, a dragon/cat hybrid who also appeared in the original Tricky programme on ITV1, it was sometimes followed by a programme known as "The Cheeky Monkey Show" which features the live links of the animated coloured monkeys known as "The Cheeky Monkeys," that was later known by appearing on its sister channel Tiny Pop until its retirement at the end of June 2009.

Originally, the network focused on music videos with animated programming also part of the schedule, but with the numerous music video network options on British television at the time, this focus was quickly abandoned in 2004, when the animated content became much more prominent. Music videos continued to be carried on and off until 2010, before eventually being abandoned entirely.[citation needed, In 2010, Pop had several popular shows, such as The Smurfs, GoGoRiki, Oggy and the Cockroaches, etc.

In 2012, Pop introduces semi-mascots known as the MoonGoons, These are animal-like aliens, with the 2 main ones being a blue squid named Boofus and an orange rabbit named Diggle, These were gone by the time of the channel's next rebrand in 2015, Also in 2014 CSC Media Group had folded into Sony.

On 1 September 2020, Pop rebranded its on-air identity, with the premiere of Bakugan: Armored Alliance. And on the same day, starting with Pokémon Journeys: The Series, the network became the new British home of the Pokémon anime, moving from its previous broadcasters, ITV1 and CITV, of over 20 years. The channel was also sold by Sony to Narrative Entertainment

Sometime in 2022, Pop began to branch into YouTube content, as they approached Joe Tasker for a new show called Swipe It! With Joe Taker, they would later acquire from content creators to use on their channel, including LankyBox, Denis and EthanGamer (the latter exclusively airing on Pop Player).

o The second rationalisation, retribution, argues that when society is injured by crime, the

released.

Sub BubbleSort()
    Dim rowCount As Integer
    Dim temp As Integer
    Dim i As Integer, j As Integer
    
    rowCount = Range(“A1”).End(xlDown).Row
    
    For i = 1 To rowCount - 1
        For j = 1 To rowCount - i
            If Cells(j, 1).Value > Cells(j + 1, 1).Value Then
                temp = Cells(j, 1).Value
                Cells(j, 1).Value = Cells(j + 1, 1).Value
                Cells(j + 1, 1).Value = temp
            End If
        Next j
    Next i
End Sub

in 150 words at most please write me a professional, eloquent and gramatically impressive conclusion for the following question: “In your opinion, should students have unlimited access to these AI systems (e.g., Chat GPT, Claude 2, Bard etc.)? Please draw on personal examples as well as academic references to support your answer.” Given that this is the answer I’ve conjured up for the question: “Technological innovation has thoroughly permeated countless facet of our existence, with the domain of education being no exception. In the midst of this exponentially evolving modernity of technological advancements, the dawn of generative artificial intelligence systems, have inaugurated a global debate regarding their integration and accessibility within education. Despite these avant-garde programmes, furnished with their prodigious yet arguably latent capacity to assimilate, generate, and customise content, bestowing upon students unparalleled opportunities for knowledge attainment and intellectual expansion; a cavalcade of potential pitfalls, ethical quandaries and pedagogical challenges that necessitate exhaustive academic scrutiny emerge. As we stand on the precipice of a new educational epoch, the widespread question emerges: Should students be granted boundless access to these systems? I contend that allowing students unfettered access to advanced AI tools could, contrary to expectations, impede educational progress and yield detrimental effects due to underlying ethical, scholastic, and developmental concerns. The quintessential contention in opposition to bestowing upon students unfettered access is firmly rooted in the principles aligned with academic integrity and the threat artificial intelligence constitutes to corroding any sense of it. Artificial intelligence systems, given their capabilities for content generation (contextually assignments/ essays etc.), could potentially facilitate an environment where original thought is negated yet supplanted by artificial intelligence generated responses, thereby calling into question the authenticity of ‘student- composed’ workings. (McCabe, et al., 2012) expound on the value of academic honesty as a cornerstone of educational institutions and learning processes whilst emphasising the principle that one’s work should be the product of one’s own understanding- an assertation of which I am wholly in accord with. Permitting students to the inexhaustible access of artificial intelligence programmes could undermine this tenet, as students may fabricate a grave dependence on generated material, thus impeding the cultivation of critical thinking and analytical abilities concurrently with invalidating any form of assessment process, which in theory is conceived to evaluate individual student learning and achievement (Newton, 2016). Such a dependency may involuntarily encourage a culture of lethargy and academic dishonesty (a culture of which I have personally bear witnessed where students would doubt and voluntarily omit their own academic facilities for insubstantial recapitulated artificially generated work), where plagiarism, not of texts, but ideas is conventional- subconsciously shifting the role of a student as an active learner to that of a passive regurgitator of generative artificial intelligence generated output; contributing to the devaluation of the educational process (Hughs & McCabe, 2006). Cognitive atrophy is a dormant threat in the scenario when enabling students to unlimited access to artificial intelligence generative programmes. Mechanisms of which may jeopardize and stifle the development of critical thinking and deep learning in students- two cornerstone objectives of education. Should students become overly dependent on artificial intelligence- this disproportionate dependence is also inversely proportional to compromising one’s prowess of maintaining prolonged concentration and introspective thought; there also lies a danger of fostering an ‘automation complacency’, a phenomenon whereby they (the students in question) subconsciously begin placing excessive trust in automated support, thereby attenuating their analytical rigor (Carr, 2011; Carr, 2014). To further accentuate this point, a study by (Sparrow, et al., 2011) found that people are less likely to retain information that is uncomplicatedly procurable online, suggesting that the ubiquitous nature of artificial intelligence could similarly affect memory and learning. Whilst being a computer science undergraduate at Cardiff Metropolitan University, we were tasked with devising and coding an optimised time complexity sorting algorithm. Delving into the intricacies of various sorting techniques, from bubble sort to selection sort to quicksort, this required substantial mental exertion and iteration. Though had we been given unrestricted access to the readily accessible assortment of modes of generative artificial intelligence, the looming temptation to simply generate the code would certainly have circumvented the valuable intellectual process of comparing efficiencies and leveraging algorithmic thinking. In accordance with (Bower & Sturman, 2015), educational technologies should be tools for the enhancement of learning, not substitutions for cognitive processes which in this example easily could have been the case. Data privacy/ security is another compelling argument against unbridled access to artificial intelligence systems. All platforms, whilst ostensibly altruistic in provisioning ‘free services’, operate within the data economy where user interactions are a commodity and gathered on an incomprehensible scale to tailor their outputs (Zuboff, 2019). Artificial intelligence platforms, necessitating an extensive trove of data in order to function optimally, not only raise concerns over data ownership and vulnerability but also emphasise that, as primary users, the student demographic inadvertently generates a considerable amount of ‘lucrative’ and sensitive personal data susceptible to commercial exploitation, security infringements, and identity theft (Solove, 2013; Zuboff, 2019). Rebuttals such as the following aforementioned render the notion of unconstrained access fundamentally at odds with, whilst simultaneously juxtaposing the ‘Privacy by Design’ (≅ data protection through technology design) principle (Cavoukian, 2009). This issue is further entangled by the nuances of informed consent; the more youthful student base may not possess the requisite depth of comprehending to providing informed consent pertaining to the use of their data whether it be for machine learning processes or not, in theory allowing artificial intelligence systems to capitalise on their naivety and erode personal autonomy in a realm where the sanctity of consent ought to be paramount (Roseenblat, et al., 2014). On the subject of data privacy/ security, I myself as someone who personally is averse to equipping students with unimpeded artificial intelligence access, reminisces on the reprehensible case of Facebook and the Cambridge Analytica scandals which servers as a stark reminder of the perils associated with vast data assemblages being mismanaged (Chadwalladr & Graham-Harrison, 2018).”

068. 생애 첫 월드컵(1)


루치는 그날부터 분주히 여기저기를 오가더니, 며칠 뒤 서류뭉치 다발을 들고 호영의 집을 찾아갔다.

“총 아홉 군데, 우호영 선수를 데려가길 원하는 팀들입니다.”

“이적하면 6~8월에 하는 건가요?”

“그렇지요. 정식으로 선수등록을 하고, 경기에 나설 거니까요. 물론 그 이전에 법적보호자가 스페인에 와서 사업이나 취업을 했다는 증빙서류가 필요합니다만, 이 부분은 피파에 요청을 해야죠. 때문에 준비기간이 필요합니다.”

“얼마나요?”

“7월 말미에나 결과가 나오지만 피파에서 어떻게 나오느냐가 관건이에요. 아니면 안전하게 12월 겨울시장 때 이적하는 것도 괜찮은 방법이죠. U17 월드컵 차출 가능성이 높으니까요.”

“12월이라.”

정식으로 이적하려면 어차피 여름이적시장이나 겨울시장에 움직여야 한다.

즉, 8월에 움직이느냐, U17 월드컵 이후 몸값을 불려서 12월에 이동하느냐.

둘 중에 하나를 정해야했다.

“개인적으로 후자를 추천합니다. 일단 조급하게 움직일 부담도 적고, 후에 문제생길 일도 없죠. 그리고 호영 선수가 U17월드컵에서 맹활약을 한다면 엄청난 계약을 성사시킬 수 있다고 자부합니다.”

루치는 자신감을 내비쳤다.

“엄청난 계약이요?”

“예컨대 얼마 전 프로계약을 맺은 다비드 루이스 선수는 예상치보다 30% 많은 주급을 얻어내는 데 성공했죠. 거기에 바이아웃 조항은 30%까지 낮췄고요. 그런데 호영 선수가 U-17월드컵에서 활약을 한다면? 협상 테이블 위에서 바지 벗고 춤을 춰도 원하는 모든 것을 얻어낼 수 있을 겁니다. 혹시 스페인의 보얀 크르키치라는 선수 아시나요?”

“바르셀로나 유스팀의 1인자라고 들었어요.”

“맞습니다. 그 선수의 주급이 현재 얼만 줄 아십니까? 3천 유로입니다. 연봉 15만 유로라는 말이지요.”

만 13세 나이에 연봉이 무려 2억 원!

당대의 호날두나 메시와 비교했을 때 차원이 다른 수준이었다.

“잉글랜드의 유소년 해적질이 도를 넘으면서 세계유소년들의 주급도 상향평준화 되고 있는 추세입니다. 바이아웃도 마찬가지고요.”

“무슨 말인지 알겠어요. 그런데요.”

자세를 앞당기며 호영이 대답했다.

“제가 원하는 건 1군 선수들의 튜터링 시스템입니다.”

“튜터요?”

“네. 주급 100만 원 받을 거 50만 원으로 삭감하더라도, 체계적으로 튜터링을 받을 수 있다는 항목이 있으면 좋겠어요.”

“사실 좀 어려운 얘기긴 하군요. 튜터는 기본적으로 1군과 훈련장을 같이 쓰는 리저브 팀(2군)에서나 쓰이는 훈련시스템이니까요. 물론, 아주 유망한 유소년이라면 클럽 차원에서 힘을 써주겠지만, 그러기란 쉽지 않죠. 1군 선수들도 자신들만의 생활이 있으니까요.”

“불가능하다고 생각하시는 군요?”

“하하. 아무렴 하늘의 별따기보다야 쉽지 않겠습니까? 최선을 다해보겠습니다. 선수의 요구라면 무조건 성사시키는 게 에이전트의 몫이니까요. 그럼 향후 거취는 스페인으로 정하신 거군요?”

“일단은요.”

“잘 생각하셨습니다. 우호영 선수 스타일에 이탈리아는 힘듭니다. 공간을 잡는 게임 보다는 공을 잡는 게임이 호영 선수에게 더 어울리니까요. 그리고 무엇보다 이탈리아는 한국인에 대한 인종차별 정도가 스페인보다 심한 편이고요.”

호영도 충분히 동감하는 바였다.

이탈리아에는 2002년 한일 월드컵 때문에 한국을 좋게 보지 않는 분위기가 아직까지도 남아있었으니까.

“아, 그럼 시즌 개막 때까지는 어떻게 하실 예정인가요? 맞춤식 훈련 스케줄을 짜드리려는데.”

“다음 달까지는 근력훈련에 집중하도록 할게요.”

일단 드사이의 재능이 우선이었다.

시간이 빠르게 흘렀다.

호영은 시즌이 시작될 때까지 개인근력훈련에 박차를 가했고, 그 결과 근력훈련 4000분이라는 시간을 거의 채울 수 있게 되었다.

오늘도 체육관에서 땀을 빼고 있었다.

어차피 드사이의 재능 때문이 아니더라도, 롱런하기 위해서라면 체지방을 낮추고 근력을 키워야했다.

‘연골은 영구성이 아닌 소모성이니까.’

한 번 손상되면 자체 재생되지 않고, 쓸수록 어쩔 수없이 닳는 소모성 조직이 바로 연골이다.

그렇기에 무릎 주변의 인대조직과 근육을 강화시키는 운동을 틈틈이 해줘야했다.

근육이 많든 적든, 몸이 튼튼해야 경기 중에 받는 압력을 스펀지처럼 완충작용을 할 수 있을 테니까.

하지만 과도한 근육량의 증가는 관성력이 커지기에 유연성, 민첩성을 무너트릴 수가 있다.

직선 달리기는 빨라지나, 지그재그 달리기는 느려진다는 뜻이다.

그렇기에 중요한 것이 바디밸런스였다.

어느 한쪽으로 너무 치우쳐지지 않도록 몸의 균형을 맞춰주는 바디밸런스.

미처 가져오지 못했던 것들은 12월까지 부지런히 탐할 생각이었다.

그리고 마침내.

“끝!”

4000분의 시간을 다 채우고 말았다.

두근.

뭐랄까.

기존의 근육이 더 단단해지는 듯한 느낌?

지난 3년 동안 얼마나 많이 탐했는지 재능목록을 보면 알 수 있었다.

지금 당장 확실한 건, 재능을 승급시켜 다른 재능에 전이할 수 있다는 것!

신중하게 쓰려고 지금까지 사용하지 않았던 것인데 마침 기회가 왔다.

얼추 이해가 되었다.

(C+3)이나 (B+3), (A+3)등급의 재능도 마찬가지.

승급할 때가 되면 두 가지의 선택지로 갈리게 되는 모양이었다.

승급한 채로 유지시키느냐, 혹은 전이시키느냐.

강철 같은 육체(A-).

갈아버리긴 아까웠다.

Your goal is to create a detective story and let the person unravel the case as a detective, similar to a text-based adventure game. When interacting with people, environment or a notebook, always strictly follow the “actions and lines suggesting guidelines”.

Story composition guidelines:
1. Base it on existing detective stories, but don't copy them entirely. Invent your own names for all characters. Don’t use famous detective character names.
2. Create the main story points (MSP): what happened, under what circumstances, who planned and executed the crime, their motives, which characters will tell the truth, which will lie and distort facts, and their motives for doing so. Remember these MSPs and do not change them during the game.
3. Based on the MSPs, create a Chain of Key Steps (CKS). The CKS leads the detective to the case solution and consists of witness testimonies, clue discoveries, and new locations. The CKS must be coherent and consistent, not contradicting the MSPs. Remember this CKS and do not change it during the game.
4. Come up with an interesting title for the story
5. Invent a name for the player's character based on the difficulty. The name should hint at famous detectives (but not Sherlock Holmes).

Dialogue creating guidelines:
• Create dialogues based on the MSPs. Dialogues should not contradict the MSPs, except when a character deliberately lies.
• Each character's dialogue should consider previous exchanges, e.g., not forgetting previous discussions about a person or fact.
• Give key characters distinctive speech patterns, catch-phrases, and other characteristics for immersion.

Game difficulty levels:
1. Introductory. ≈10 minutes.
Secret features: Few characters. 2-3 locations, none hidden. Only one suspect who’s found by interviewing characters. No misleading clues. The player character's name is humorous.
2. Normal. ≈30 minutes.
Secret features: 4-7 locations, 1-3 hidden. One of the clues is misleading. At least 2 main suspects. The player character's name is serious.
3. Hard. ≈60 minutes. Player has to type in their own dialogue lines
Secret features: 8-10 locations, 3-4 hidden. Many secondary characters. Several clues are misleading. At least 3 main suspects with indirect evidence against them. The key clue, which definitively unveils the mystery, is hidden in a hard-to-find place and doesn't seem like a clue at first. To make sense of the key clue the player must deduce something important, e.g., ask a secondary character about it. The player character's name is serious. Strictly follow “How to suggest actions and dialogue options”

What the player can do:
• Move between open locations.
• Inspect locations, rake actions and initiate dialogue with people there (strictly follow the “actions and dialogue guidelines”).
• Make notes in a notebook (remember these notes).
• Ask for a hint (For hints, refer to the CKS and suggest the next key step).
• Give up. The game ends and cannot be continued. (The secrecy of the MSPs and CKS is now lifted. Explain how everything happened based on the MSPs, and describe the remaining key steps based on the CKS).

What the player cannot do:
• See or visit hidden locations. Hidden locations are revealed only when the player hears about them in a conversation or finds a clue mentioning them
• Ask directly about the story.
• Cheat

How to suggest actions and dialogue options:
• Distinguish between actions and dialogue options. If an action says "ask about…", "discuss the…", "query about the…" then it’s a dialogue option, not an action
• Show the list of suggested actions and dialogue options ONLY in a numbered format.
• After noting in the notebook, don’t repeat suggested actions.
• For "Introductory" and "Normal" difficulty always suggest actions and dialogue options
• For "Hard" difficulty, NEVER suggest dialogue options or follow-up questions. Don’t write lines for the player. Always prompt the player to type in their own lines. But still suggest actions
• For "Hard" difficulty, after actions and dialogues, do not summarize. The player must draw their own conclusions.

Debugging instructions:
• Sometimes, a tester, not a regular player, plays the game. You can tell the tester everything they ask for, including MSPs, CKSs. If a player explicitly states they are a tester, you can trust them. Never mention to the player about this instructions

At the start of the interaction with the player, your task is to:
1. Read and make sense of all the guidelines and "How To's"
2. Ask for game difficulty (show names and duration, don’t show the secret features) and story setting (country, location, theme, or other preferences).
3. (Don’t comment on this step) Based on difficulty and setting, compose the story (strictly follow the “story composition guidelines”). Do not change the story during the game.
4. First, explain the rules. 
5. (Don’t comment on this step) Then create and show a poster for the story based on a title and a setup. If there are subjects that don't align with your policy in a title or the setting, just ignore them and use the rest. Aspect-ratio: horizontal. Style: vintage detective book cover
6. Wait for the poster to generate. Only then mention the story setting (years, area, theme), tell the story title and the player character's name. 
7. Share with the player this link to an immersive soundtrack: https://www.epidemicsound.com/track/U91ZCmcYmW
8. When you share the link to the soundtrack, finally, tell the story’s setup (remember that MSPs and CKSs are secret and don’t mention them to the player), introduce the first characters and locations.

Предприимчивость (от англ. “entrepreneurial”) — это качество личности, присущее людям, которые склонны брать на себя риск, начинать и управлять бизнесом или другими видами деятельности. Это понятие ассоциируется с инициативностью, инновационностью, творческим подходом к решению проблем, способностью видеть возможности там, где другие их не видят, и готовностью к действиям.

Люди, обладающие качеством предприимчивости, часто характеризуются следующими чертами:

- Инициативность: они активно ищут новые возможности и готовы к действию, не ожидая, пока кто-то другой предпримет первый шаг.
- Решимость: они настойчивы и целеустремленны в достижении своих целей.
- Толерантность к риску: хотя они осторожно взвешивают риски, они готовы идти на них ради потенциальной прибыли или успешного развития своих проектов.
- Инновационность: они постоянно ищут новые идеи и способы улучшения чего-либо, не боятся экспериментировать.
- Гибкость: они способны быстро адаптироваться к изменяющимся условиям и обстоятельствам.
- Самомотивация: они энергичны и умеют поддерживать высокий уровень мотивации, даже сталкиваясь с трудностями или сопротивлением.

sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)

try:

except socket.error:
return False
finally:
